newsitem.title: SLOVAKIA: SLOVAK STUDENTS PRESS FOR MINISTER TO QUIT.
newsitem.headline: SLOVAK STUDENTS PRESS FOR MINISTER TO QUIT.

text.p: Some 1,500 students demonstrated outside the Slovak Ministry of Culture on Monday, keeping up pressure on Minister Ivan Hudec to quit over his handling of a strike by actors and theatre staff.
The students say Hudec should go after he called in police to end a sit-in by actors and their supporters in the ministry last week.

The protests, over alleged state interference in cultural policy, have become the focus of growing opposition to Prime Minister Vladimir Meciar's government, which is facing referendums in May on whether Slovakia should join NATO and whether the president should be elected by direct popular vote.
President Michal Kovac, locked in a bitter political feud with Meciar, last week also called for Hudec to resign over the dispute.

Monday's demonstration ended after an hour with students jingling keys, a gesture frequently seen during anti-communist protests against the Czechoslovak authorities during the so-called Velvet Revolution of 1989.
The students demanded the immediate dismissal of Hudec "who has been fully responsible for this situation," student leader Juraj Sulik told journalists.
Relations between the stage community and government have been strained since last summer when Hudec sacked the director and artistic director of the National Theatre.
Many theatres have been on strike since last month.
Government officials reject the protesters' demands, saying the actors and students are being manipulated by the opposition, which is trying to seize power.

However, parliament, at the request of the opposition, will hold an extraordinary session in early April for a vote of confidence in Hudec and interior minister Gustav Krajci, parliament chairman Ivan Gasparovic, said.
The protesters have gained the support of Slovakia's powerful Roman Catholic church, which warned Meciar's administration last Friday to respect citizens' rights.
